previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with advanced HIV/AIDS, chronic respiratory failure, and recent right hip fracture repair was admitted from a rehab facility with fever, tachypnea, and respiratory distress. He was found to have healthcare-associated pneumonia with gram-negative bacteria, likely from his recent hospitalization. He required mechanical ventilation initially due to worsening secretions and hypoxia. Bronchoscopy with mini-BAL confirmed gram-negative rods, and he was treated with intravenous antibiotics, initially broad-spectrum and later narrowed to ceftazidime. His respiratory status improved over the course of the admission, allowing weaning from mechanical ventilation to trach mask support. He remained lethargic but arousable, with stable neurologic status and no seizures. He completed an 8-day course of antibiotics and was discharged to extended care with plans for ongoing tracheostomy care, physical therapy, and follow-up with multiple specialists, including for evaluation of mediastinal widening noted on imaging.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  CT HEAD W/O CONTRAST

INDICATION:  History: ___ with HIV, pulling out G tube. Unable to provide much
of history  // evaluate for trauma, infection. Patient also pulled out G-tube
3x in last week.

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous multidetector CT scan through the head was performed
without intravenous contrast.  Axial images displayed as separate 5 mm and 2.5
mm bone algorithm image series.  Multiplanar reformation was performed to
construct coronal and sagittal images.

DOSE:  DLP:  891.93 mGy-cm.   CTDIvol:  54.53 mGy.

COMPARISON:  MRI from ___. CT from ___.

FINDINGS: 

There is no evidence of fracture, hemorrhage, edema, mass effect, or
infarction.  There is ex vacuo dilation of the bilateral lateral ventricles
and third ventricle, more severe on the right, unchanged from prior studies
and related to cerebral volume loss.  There are coarse calcifications in the
left temporal lobe and bilateral basal ganglia, new since the previous study. 
These are likley sequelae of prior infection. Extensive white matter
hypodensities are unchanged.  The imaged paranasal sinuses, mastoid air cells,
and middle ear cavities are clear.

IMPRESSION: 

No acute intracranial abnormality. Evidence of diffuse cerebral atrophy and
sequela of prior infection.

EXAMINATION:  CT C-SPINE W/O CONTRAST

INDICATION:  History:  ___ M with HIV, pulling out G tube. Unable to provide
much of history. Evaluate for trauma, infection. Patient also pulled out
G-tube 3x in last week.

TECHNIQUE:  Non-contrast multidetector helical CT scan through the cervical
spine was performed.  Image data processed to generate 2.5 mm axial soft
tissue algorithm, 2.5 mm axial bone algorithm, coronal, and sagittal image
series.

DOSE:  DLP: 758.82  mGy-cm;   CTDIvol: ___ MGy.

COMPARISON:  None available.

FINDINGS: 

There is no evidence of fracture or alignment abnormality.  There is no
prevertebral soft tissue swelling.  Limited, non-contrast appearance of the
included soft tissues is unremarkable.  No concerning abnormality is seen in
the included upper lungs.  CT is not able to provide intrathecal detail
comparable to MRI; within this limitation, the outline of the thecal sac
appears normal.

IMPRESSION: 

Normal study.

EXAMINATION:  CT TORSO W/CONTRAST

INDICATION:  History:  ___ M with HIV, pulling out G tube. Unable to provide
much of history. Evaluate for trauma, infection. Patient also pulled out
G-tube 3x in last week.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT acquired axial images of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis were
obtained after administration of 130 mL Omnipaque intravenous contrast.
Enteric contrast was not given. Coronal and sagittal reformats prepared and
reviewed.

DOSE:  DLP:  767.38 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  Chest CT from ___. CT abdomen and pelvis from ___.

FINDINGS: 

CHEST:

The imaged thyroid is normal. There is no axillary, supraclavicular,
mediastinal, or hilar lymphadenopathy by CT size criteria. The heart is
structurally normal and there is no pericardial effusion. There is minimal
diffuse ground-glass opacity superimposed on global, chronic, diffuse
background changes of the lung parenchyma consisting of interstitial
abnormality with both peripheral and peribronchovascular distribution, as well
as subpleural foci of fibrosis. The airways are patent.  There is an
unremarkable tracheostomy tube in place. There are no concerning pulmonary
nodules. There is no pneumothorax or pleural effusion.

ABDOMEN:

The liver enhances homogeneously, without concerning focal lesion. There are
gallstones in a noninflamed gallbladder. The pancreas is normal, without focal
lesion or duct dilation. The spleen is normal in size, without focal lesion.
The adrenal glands are normal. The kidneys enhance normally and excrete
contrast briskly. There are no solid renal lesions or hydronephrosis. There is
a well-positioned gastrostomy tube in place. The stomach and duodenum are
otherwise normal. The small bowel and large bowel are normal in caliber,
without wall thickening or mass.  There is evidence of prior bowel resection
with an anastomosis in the right lower quadrant.

There is no intra- or retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy. There is no ascites,
fluid collection, or pneumoperitoneum. The abdominal aorta is normal caliber,
with patent main branches. Portal vein and IVC are patent.

PELVIS:

The urinary bladder is without wall thickening or mass.  There is a Foley
catheter in place. The rectum is unremarkable. There is no pelvic mass. There
is no free fluid. There is no pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy. The prostate
and seminal vesicles are unremarkable.

BONES AND SOFT TISSUES:

There is no acute fracture.  There are bilateral hip fractures status post
ORIF. There are no destructive osseous lesions concerning for malignancy or
infection. There are no soft tissue masses.

IMPRESSION:


1. Mild pulmonary edema on a background of diffuse severe chronic lung
disease.
2. Gastrostomy tube appears well positioned.
3. No acute process in the chest abdomen or pelvis. No acute fracture or other
evidence of acute traumatic injury.

EXAMINATION:  HIP UNILAT MIN 2 VIEWS RIGHT

INDICATION:  ___ man, complaining of hip pain after fall. Evaluate for
fracture.

COMPARISON:  Hip radiographs from ___.

FINDINGS: 

The patient is status post ORIF of a right femoral intertrochanteric fracture,
which has healed. The hardware is intact and there is no evidence of hardware
related complication. There is no acute fracture or dislocation. Sclerosis
right femoral head compatible with avascular necrosis (unchanged).

IMPRESSION: 

Healed intertrochanteric fracture of the right femur, status post ORIF.  No
evidence of hardware-related complication or acute fracture.

EXAMINATION:  CHEST (PORTABLE AP)

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with HIV/AIDS, COPD, s/p trach w increased
secretions.  // Eval for pneumonia

COMPARISON:  ___

IMPRESSION: 

As compared to the previous radiograph, no relevant change is seen. The lung
volumes remain low. The parenchymal opacities at the right and left lung base,
likely reflecting pneumonia, are unchanged in extent and severity.  No new
opacities are visualized. Borderline size of the cardiac silhouette without
pulmonary edema. The tracheostomy tube is constant in appearance.
